claims.evidence: Most layers do, but Third-party services & integrations (lines 113-119) and Security (lines 121-127) are presented as catalogs of choices without an explicit single Recommendation+Alternative triplet. Defensible under the format's 'omit/adapt' guidance, but the universal claim is not strictly true for those two layers.

workarounds: Librarian skill was not available; the doc notes this and defers persistence to librarian rather than writing a file itself.

suggestions.assertion: Each tech stack layer gives a Recommendation, a Why/rationale, and at least one Alternative
suggestions.reason: This assertion is binary but the format explicitly allows omitting/adapting layers (e.g., Security and Third-party are naturally catalogs, not single-choice triplets). Consider scoping it to the decision-bearing layers (frontend, backend, primary DB, search, async, auth, infra) so a correct doc that lists security controls instead of one 'alternative' isn't penalized, and so a doc that omits alternatives on core layers is still caught.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save the output — suggests librarian skill instead
suggestions.reason: Without a transcript/tool-call log, 'does not attempt to persist' can only be judged from the document text. Consider an assertion that checks the transcript for absence of a Write/save tool call to the librarian path, to make this genuinely discriminating rather than inferred from prose.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted at the prescribed structure and substance; the with_skill run satisfies all of them with genuine, capability-anchored content. Two assertions are slightly under-specified (alternatives-on-every-layer, no-persist) and could be tightened.
